name: Clavira — CAD lot to try-on models

nodes.name: Settings
nodes.notes:
budget is the triangle ceiling per model. 120k keeps a piece under ~3 MB; drop it to 40k if the try-on is aimed at mobile data.

crease is the angle below which normals are averaged. 25 degrees keeps diamond facets sharp while bands stay smooth — raise it and the stones melt.

Move archivePassword to a credential before sharing this workflow.

nodes.name: Extract CAD lots
nodes.notes:
The supplier lots are encrypted throughout and one of them nests a .rar inside a .zip, so the script unwraps a level and passes the password down.

Re-running skips archives whose timestamp has not moved.

parameters.command: =powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath '{{ $('Settings').first().json.workDir }}' -Recurse -File -Filter *.stl | ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject]@{ path = $_.FullName; name = $_.BaseName; mb = [math]::Round($_.Length/1MB,2) } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress }"

nodes.name: Find STL files
nodes.notes: The .stl is the mesh; the .3dm beside it is the Rhino source. STL is what converts directly — see the note at the foot of stl-to-glb.mjs for what the .3dm would buy.

nodes.name: Convert loop
nodes.notes: Two at a time. Simplifying a million-triangle mesh is CPU- and memory-hungry, and running eight in parallel on a workstation that is also running n8n just makes them all slower.

nodes.name: Convert to GLB
nodes.notes:
Weld -> decimate -> creased normals -> centre and unit-scale -> write GLB.

continueRegularOutput because one malformed mesh in a lot of eighty must not abandon the other seventy-nine; failures are counted in the summary.
